mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply chain, which leads to reduced output and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of supply chain weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a shift towards consumer-driven growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of consumer-driven growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over six months signals inflationary pressure, which erodes real returns and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month, it signals strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong job growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds 3%, it signals robust economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
